angle: One process and its regimes, said without poles. The region is read as ONE loop: something is picked by a rule; what is picked has a hand in the rule and in who judges how the rule is doing. Three questions sort its regimes: (1) where the rule comes from (outside its results / from them / from them and held); (2) who is among those the rule is judged through (someone standing apart, only those not favoured, nobody, or those who would notice already removed); (3) whether what the loop uses up outside what it counts reaches a judge, and before or after it can still turn. "Held for one side" and "held the other way" are ONE place (holding) with a dividing line; crossings are arrows from the place to itself. AI-written proposal; read-only, nothing in the repository changed.

Items in scope: 88 = 59 exits + 23 transitions + 6 compose entries (counted by script over dynamics.json). Assigned: arrows 69 items (70 rows: reading-a-loss-in-time transition 1 is an exact threshold with two destinations and has two rows); held_by 5 items (readings-revised exit 1 and exit 3, unselected exit 11, loss-read-in-time transition 3, readings-revised compose 1); unresolved 14 (11 exits, 3 transitions). 69 + 5 + 14 = 88. Of the 70 arrow rows: 21 exact, 13 sufficient or bound, 2 necessary, 17 witness, 14 reading or argued, 1 open, 2 proved joins (rows may carry two marks). 18 rows are from holding to itself (crossing or dividing its two sides). Five dynamics have no exit, transition or compose and enter only as held_by or as a marked place: target-capture, a-reading-against-the-share-does-not-ratchet, capture-reaching-the-routes-of-correction, selection-for-narrowing-what-couples-in, self-reproducing-selection-across-carriers. The other held_by lines under each place are staying laws from the dynamics' own mechanisms and are not among the 88. Not counted: two compose entries that point INTO offspring-read-from-giving-that-waits from dynamics outside the scope (what-a-rise-draws-from-beyond, what-decides-giving-against-keeping-on-a-flow). what_the_layer_shows:
(1) WHAT CONNECTS. The region is two tracks that meet. Track one, where the rule comes from: rule-apart <-> winners-set-rule (seven exact thresholds, all one question: does setting the rule return more to the setters alone than it costs) -> holding (within two rounds) -> all-on-one (by chance). Track two, what is used up outside and who registers it: uncounted -> felt (exact: when it touches a judge) -> holding on the other side, or past-turning-back (exact, by the numbers when it is registered). The centre, judged-inside, is where holding and uncounted coincide. Its proved lines: IN from winners-set-rule (held within two rounds from any start); OUT to cost-counts (sufficient, twice) and to felt (exact, named model). So the diagnosis's 'the meta-attractor has no line in or out' is repaired by this layer for three lines.

(2) HOLES WORTH DRAWING AS HOLES. (a) Every arrow that says how the judges come to be inside or gone is a reading or open: cost-counts -> judged-inside (two readings: nothing holds an outside judge in place; dropping one can win), noticers-gone -> judged-inside (one reading, one explicitly open: the join of 'rule-setting gains ground' with 'measured among those left' is not made). That open arrow is the centre of the concern, and it is one dashed line. (b) Nothing says how a rule set apart comes to be rebuilt from its results: the thresholds between rule-apart and winners-set-rule are exact, but 'the rule follows the lead' enters every holding law as a premise. (c) Out of felt, the general laws stop: 'which way it then turns is not stated', 'told apart, not responded to'. Only the named pool model continues. Four exits that go on from felt (the difference made up; each takes all it can; the others outrun the renewal) leave the region unresolved: a place 'acted on / made up again' is missing here. (d) cost-counts has no law that keeps a run in it beyond its own premise (the judge stays whatever the lead); its only out-arrows are readings back to the centre. (e) The codes (several-ways, all-on-one) are an island on the rule track: eight arrows among themselves, joined to the rest only at all-on-one (from holding by chance, from noticers-gone by removal). No datum joins 'several ways in use' to 'winners help set the rule': the code laws have no rule that follows the lead. 'A language settling on one word is the same loop as a monopoly' is not yet a join in the atlas. (f) No settled state: one staying law (a rule rebuilt against the lead does not ratchet), the 'one round between, either way' of the timing law (open), and a swinging witness that lives in family F. (g) ended is reached by one exact threshold and three examples; past-turning-back -> ended is an example only. (h) checkers-inside and outlives-members have no arrows at all. (i) Chance: holding -> all-on-one is proved only for members replaced one at a time; for counts that only grow (a habit) the entry cites that chance does not leave it.

(3) WHAT A PERSON WOULD SEE. Holding has 18 arrows to itself and absorbs seven dynamics: most of family C's theorems are about one place and its dividing line. Uncounted absorbs family B's two largest dynamics (16 items). The news of the region is thin and sits on the arrows between places, most of them not yet laws.

(4) GROWTH. Places that would also be places elsewhere: ended (every family; one shared node), all-on-one (A fixation, D, G), holding (D, G, A basins), past-turning-back (A, B), uncounted (B's home), felt and cost-counts (05's pools, regulation in 02 section 8), several-ways (any symmetric start), noticers-gone (survivorship in D and H). Places this region shows are missing elsewhere: 'still going on within what renews it' (H; persisting-filters belongs there), 'drawing past what renews it' (A/B), 'the difference made up again' (02 section 7), 'swinging with no settled side' (F), 'aiming at enough' (D).
layout:
A page read left to right as 'how much of the rule comes from its own results', in three horizontal bands that are not better or worse: top band = ways in use; middle band = the rule and its results; bottom band = what lies outside the count and who stands there. Suggested grid (x 0-12 left to right, y 0-8 top to bottom).
TOP BAND: several-ways (1.5, 1) ... all-on-one (11, 1), joined by one bundle of arrows straight across.
MIDDLE BAND: rule-apart (1.5, 4) - winners-set-rule (4.5, 4) - holding (7.5, 4), drawn as a twin-lobed node with a visible dividing line between its two sides; the 18 self-arrows become one double-headed arc across that line, labelled with what carries a run across (a moved count, a reversed rule held one round, a change in what is rewarded taken up at once). judged-inside is drawn INSIDE holding as an inner region (it is holding plus two more conditions), on the lobe nearer the bottom band. noticers-gone (10.5, 4) sits to the right of holding, directly under all-on-one, so its arrow up to all-on-one is short.
BOTTOM BAND: uncounted (2.5, 7) under rule-apart (a fixed measure is where family B's laws live); felt (6, 6.5) below and left of holding; cost-counts (8.5, 7.5) below holding; past-turning-back (11, 6.5) at the right. Putting cost-counts in the same band as uncounted is deliberate: both are about the outside, and neither band is the good one.
ended is not a node in the field: draw it as the right-hand edge of the page (x = 12.5), reached from past-turning-back, noticers-gone and (a long arrow along the bottom margin) uncounted; other families will reach the same edge.
checkers-inside (a reading) is a dashed label sitting ON the two dashed arrows from cost-counts up to judged-inside, since it names that passage. outlives-members (open) is a dotted ring around holding, judged-inside and noticers-gone, with no arrows.
Line style carries how far seen: solid = exact, sufficient or necessary law; solid thin with a dot = witness (one example); dashed = reading or argued; dotted with '?' = open (noticers-gone -> judged-inside). Blank areas to leave blank and label: between several-ways and winners-set-rule (no join); to the right of felt toward a missing 'made up again'; around cost-counts (nothing keeps it).
Crossings: the long arrows uncounted -> noticers-gone (three, bundle them) cross the felt -> holding bundle once; uncounted -> cost-counts passes under felt; everything else runs between neighbours. No arrow needs to cross the top band.
doubts:
Least sure, and what I would argue against in my own proposal:
1. One place for both sides of a hold. I made 'held for one side' and 'held the other way' one place (the chapter itself says it is 'the same closed reading'), so 18 arrows run from holding to itself and two parameter conditions (one side or two; which side an even split favours) stay unresolved inside it. A proposer who splits holding into 'one side only' and 'two sides, the start decides' would resolve those two and match my own angle's third question better; I did not, to keep the count down and avoid naming a side.
2. judged-inside, holding and uncounted overlap: a run at the centre is in all three. I draw the centre nested inside holding. One could instead drop uncounted as a place and treat it as a property; I kept it because family B's two largest dynamics need a home.
3. past-turning-back and felt each merge a general law of family B (what is lost can no longer be kept; a difference reaches a judge) with a named-model law of family C (the hold can no longer be turned; the others register the loss). The only data joining them is one compose entry and one exit, both readings. If that reading fails these are four places.
4. The family E items. I put offspring transitions 1 and 2 and both proved compose entries on the threshold rule-apart <-> winners-set-rule. The join is proved, but 'pairs who give back' are not in any plain sense 'winners with a hand in the rule'. This is the fit I trust least; they may belong to E's own places with a single join line into this region.
5. rule-apart also receives 'rule-setters lose ground' (nothing_back_falls, and the lower side of the thresholds). That the rule is then 'set apart from winners' is a small step of mine, not a law.
6. cost-counts merges three regimes the chapter lists separately (a limit; a judge standing apart; the cost falling on those ahead). 'Falls on those ahead' may deserve its own place: it is the only way out that needs no judge.
7. the-lock-draws-its-readers-out transition 1 is drawn from holding; it could as well leave from judged-inside or uncounted (before removal the would-be noticers are present but have not registered anything).
8. noticers-gone and judged-inside may be one place reached two ways (by make-up, by removal). I kept two because their arrows between are exactly the reading and the open join, and that hole should be visible.
9. Words. 'Cost' in a label ('The cost counts') and 'winners', 'ahead' are not fully neutral: the entries say what is used up is 'a count the loop does not read; that it is a loss is a significance's to say'. Glosses say 'what is used up'; the labels do not. 'Past turning back' replaces the six-word 'past the point of no return' only to meet the five-word limit.
